text: Estimates of English's entropy fall from 4.7 bits per letter to about 1. Why?
choices: Longer texts have more repetition, so the estimate falls as the sample grows.
English has been simplifying over time, so modern text is more predictable than older text.
Conditional entropy: H(X|Y) ≤ H(X), so accounting for more context leaves less surprise to measure.
The earlier estimates included punctuation and spaces, which the later ones exclude.
explanation: 4.7 ignoring frequency, 4.1 with letter frequencies, 3.5 with pairs, about 1 with real context — Shannon's own figure from guessing experiments. The information was always about that low; the earlier estimates were not looking at enough. This is also why a system that predicts the next symbol well is a good compressor: prediction and compression are the same problem.
